name: Harvest Keeper
rootCause: According to news, the Harvest_Keeper project maliciously transferred user funds, involving an amount of about 933,000 US dollars. Through the data on the chain, it was found that the attacker used the owner authority to transfer the USDT pledged by the user in the HarvestKeeper contract by calling the getAmount function, and then the attacker used the user's token authorization to the EOA account to transfer the user's funds through the EOA multiple times.

descriptions.text: According to news, the Harvest_Keeper project maliciously transferred user funds, involving an amount of about 933,000 US dollars. Through the data on the chain, it was found that the attacker used the owner authority to transfer the USDT pledged by the user in the HarvestKeeper contract by calling the getAmount function, and then the attacker used the user's token authorization to the EOA account to transfer the user's funds through the EOA multiple times.

Harvest said that USDC, USDT, and WETH Vault were affected because of the use of Idle. Currently Harvest has not explained how to deal with it, and reminds users not to interact with these vaults until the problem is resolved.

Harvest Keeper, an AI-themed DeFi dApp, carried out a rug pull on or around 19 March 2023, draining user deposits and approved funds totaling roughly $930,000. Privileged admin functions and deceptive ice phishing attacks were used across Ethereum and other chains. Harvest Keeper's team exploited privileged smart contract functions to drain user deposits, while also leveraging user approval permissions via ice phishing. The lack of on-chain controls and unrestricted admin access enabled both direct drain and user-targeted asset theft.
